'And in the seventh week in the first year thereof, in this jubilee, Noah planted vines on the mountain on which the ark had rested, named Lubar, one of the Ararat Mountains, and they produced fruit in the fourth year, and he guarded their fruit, and gathered it in this year in the seventh month.' Noah as first vintner — the post-flood new order includes WINE, a creaturely good destined for Eucharistic transposition. **Tewahedo reading**: Tewahedo eucharistic practice retains the Noahic-creaturely register through use of locally-produced wine; the vine's appearance in Jub 7:1 grounds the Tewahedo treatment of viticulture as part of the priestly economy.

'And Canaan saw the nakedness of his father Ham, and he went out and told his two brethren who were without.' Canaan, not Ham himself, is the verse's actor — Jubilees clarifies the narrative ambiguity of Gen 9:22. **Tewahedo Hamitic-identity anchor (paired with Jub 9:13)**: the curse falls on Canaan (a specific bloodline) not on Ham (the broader descent). The Tewahedo reading is explicit: there is NO racial curse on the Hamitic descendants generally; the curse is bounded, juridical, and limited to Canaan's line. This is a sharp Tewahedo distinctive against the Western 'curse of Ham' racialisation.

'And in the twenty-eighth jubilee Noah began to enjoin upon his sons' sons the ordinances and commandments, and all the judgments that he knew, and he exhorted his sons to observe righteousness.' 'For owing to these three things came the flood upon the earth, namely, owing to the fornication wherein the Watchers against the law of their ordinances went a whoring after the daughters of men, and took themselves wives of all which they chose; and they made the beginning of uncleanness.' 'For I see, and behold the demons have begun (their) seductions against you and against your children — and now I fear on your behalf, that after my death ye will shed the blood of men upon the earth, and that ye, too, will be destroyed from the face of the earth.' 'And ye also, my children, observe the commandments of your father Enoch, and eat no blood, and observe the path of righteousness.' Noah cites his great-grandfather ENOCH as a normative source for his sons — Enoch is preached as PRE-MOSAIC patristic authority. **Tewahedo inter-canonical witness**: Jubilees and 1 Enoch mutually authorise each other within the Tewahedo canon — Jubilees cites Enoch (here and at 21:10), and 1 Enoch grounds the cosmology Jubilees presupposes. This mutual citation is unique to the Tewahedo/Eritrean Orthodox biblical structure.
